cf.title: WITHOUT OVERLAPS foreign key allows referencing EXCLUDE constraint

input.subject: WITHOUT OVERLAPS foreign key allows referencing EXCLUDE constraint

verdict_reasoning: The fix closes a correctness hole reported by a committer, and no objection survived at levels 1a or 1b. Two fixable level 2 points remain about back-branch behaviour: standards-compat-1 (a dump from an earlier 18.x fails to restore the foreign key on a fixed 18.x) and standards-compat-2 (the 18-only warning assumes the fix lands before 19.0). Both are release-policy choices that a committer who knows back-patching practice has to settle.

brief.title: Forbid temporal foreign keys that reference plain exclusion constraints
brief.problem: A foreign key with PERIOD can reference a plain EXCLUDE constraint, which does not guarantee uniqueness and whose updates do not conflict with FOR KEY SHARE. This allows serialization anomalies, as Andres Freund reported. Users of temporal foreign keys in 18.x are affected.
brief.proposed_design: The patch requires the referenced index to have indisunique as well as indisexclusion, so only WITHOUT OVERLAPS primary keys and unique constraints qualify. pg_upgrade gains a check for existing bad foreign keys. A second, REL_18_STABLE-only commit warns when the server builds an RI plan for such a foreign key or clones one to a new partition.
user_visible_surface: New error when a temporal foreign key references an exclusion constraint or a primary key without WITHOUT OVERLAPS.
New pg_upgrade check that reports temporal foreign keys referencing non-unique indexes.
New warning in 18.x when the server uses or clones such a foreign key.
Restoring a pg_dump from 18.x that contains such a foreign key fails on fixed versions.
author_claims: A temporal foreign key that references a WITHOUT OVERLAPS key already conflicts with FOR KEY SHARE, so it has no anomaly.
Few users likely created temporal foreign keys on plain exclusion constraints.
A primary key without WITHOUT OVERLAPS already failed before, but with an unhelpful error.
Fixing this before 19 is released limits the warning code to the 18 branch.
A catalog query, proposed for the release notes, finds affected foreign keys.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. The author asks whether to add the fix to the 19 Open Items list, and Peter Eisentraut is listed as reviewer in the CommitFest.
unclear: The material does not show the new error message texts or the pg_upgrade report format.
The proposal does not say whether pg_dump could warn or rewrite such foreign keys instead of failing at restore.
The proposal does not say how often the 18.x warning fires, for example once per plan or once per session.
No documentation change is listed for the restriction on referenced constraints.
search_queries: FOR KEY SHARE serialization anomaly foreign key

prior_attempts.title: Revert temporal primary keys and foreign keys
prior_attempts.quote: This feature set did not handle empty ranges correctly, and it's now too late for PostgreSQL 17 to fix it.
prior_attempts.reason:
This feature set did not handle empty ranges correctly, and it's now
too late for PostgreSQL 17 to fix it.

The following commits are reverted:

    6db4598fcb8 Add stratnum GiST support function
    46a0cd4cefb Add temporal PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints
    86232a49a43 Fix comment on gist_stratnum_btree
    030e10ff1a3 Rename pg_constraint.conwithoutoverlaps to conperiod
    a88c800deb6 Use daterange and YMD in without_overlaps tests instead of tsrange.
    5577a71fb0c Use half-open interval notation in without_overlaps tests
    34768ee3616 Add temporal FOREIGN KEY contraints
    482e108cd38 Add test for REPLICA IDENTITY with a temporal key
    c3db1f30cba doc:  clarify PERIOD and WITHOUT OVERLAPS in CREATE TABLE
    144c2ce0cc7 Fix ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING/UPDATE for temporal indexes
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 reverted temporal keys because they mishandled empty ranges. This patch closes a remaining gap of that kind: a temporal foreign key could reference a plain EXCLUDE constraint, which does not reject empty ranges.

objections.title: Back-patched error breaks dump and restore within the 18.x series
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 18.1 has a temporal foreign key on a plain exclusion constraint and dumps the database. They restore it into 18.3, which has the fix. pg_restore reports an error for that constraint and continues, so the table loads without the foreign key, and the user may notice only if they read the error output.
objections.argument: Patch 0001 is marked Backpatch-through: 18, and its commit message says restoring such keys fails. The usual expectation is that a dump taken on a minor release restores on a later minor release of the same branch. Patch 0002 adds a warning on 18, but the warning appears only on the source server and does not prevent the restore failure. A committer would likely ask whether 18 should reject only new definitions and keep accepting existing ones, for example during restore, while 19 and later reject them outright.
objections.author_must_show: Why should 18.x reject these definitions at restore time instead of warning, given that a dump from an earlier 18.x release then loses the foreign key?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 and both commit messages confirm that restoring such a key fails on a fixed 18.x, and only pg_upgrade gets a check. The proposal does not weigh the alternative of rejecting these keys only from 19 on.

objections.title: Warning code is limited to 18, but 19.0 may already allow these keys
objections.failure_scenario: If 19.0 ships before the fix, a user on 19.0 can create such a key. After a minor update to 19.1, the server neither warns nor checks. The key keeps allowing serialization anomalies, and the user finds out only at the next dump or major upgrade.
objections.argument: Message #1 limits the warning to 18 because the fix is expected to land before 19 is released. The CommitFest entry targets 18, it is still in Needs review, and the review date is after the usual major release window. If 19.0 has shipped, the reasoning behind the 18-only split in patch 0002 no longer holds, and the 19 branch would need the warning as well.
objections.author_must_show: If 19.0 ships without the fix, will patch 0002 also go to REL_19_STABLE, or what else warns users with keys created on 19.0?

critic.reasoning: The material does not say whether 19.0 has shipped, so the scenario is conditional. Patch 0002 states that later branches see such keys only from 18.x, and that stops being true if 19.0 shipped without the fix.

refuted.title: Backpatched error makes 18.x dumps unrestorable on later 18.x minors
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on 18.2 has a temporal foreign key on an exclusion constraint and updates to the fixed 18.x minor. Later they restore a dump, or seed a logical replication subscriber with pg_dump --schema-only, and the ADD CONSTRAINT fails. Default pg_restore keeps going, so the target runs without that foreign key, and they notice only if they read the error log.
refuted.argument: 0001 carries Backpatch-through: 18, so the new error also fires inside the 18 branch, and 0002 states that restoring from an old pg_dump will fail. The pg_upgrade check covers only pg_upgrade. Dump/restore and logical-replication upgrades get only a release-note query and a runtime warning. A committer would likely ask whether a minor release may make same-major dumps fail, when 18 could warn and 19 could reject.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should the 18 branch reject new such foreign keys instead of only warning, given that existing 18.x dumps and schema copies then fail to restore on a later 18.x minor?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The logical replication case is the same failed ADD CONSTRAINT during a schema restore.

refuted.title: Warning on RI plan build repeats in every backend in 18.x
refuted.failure_scenario: A site on 18.x has one affected foreign key and uses many short-lived connections. After the minor update, each new backend that inserts into the referencing table builds the RI plan and emits the warning. Clients and the server log see the same warning thousands of times a day.
refuted.argument: The 0002 commit message says the warning fires when the server builds an RI plan. RI plans are cached per backend, so with frequent reconnects the warning repeats each time and lands in both client output and the log. Postgres usually avoids new noisy client-facing messages in minor releases, so a committer would likely ask for a bounded rate or a different place to warn. The proposal does not say how often the warning fires.
refuted.author_must_show: How often does the 18.x warning fire under connection pooling, and why is warning at RI plan build better than a one-time check such as amcheck-style tooling or the release-note query?

critic.reasoning: The warning reaches only sites that have a foreign key that cannot reliably enforce referential integrity, and it stops once they replace the key. Rubric item 8 concerns cost for non-users, who pay nothing here; warning frequency is an implementation detail.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 adds a pg_upgrade check in check.c for temporal foreign keys that reference non-unique indexes.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch narrows which constraints a foreign key with PERIOD may reference; no new syntax.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A dump from 18.x that contains such a foreign key fails to restore that constraint on fixed versions.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 is marked Backpatch-through: 18, and patch 0002 is for REL_18_STABLE only.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The 18 branch carries warning code in ri_triggers.c and tablecmds.c, and pg_upgrade carries a new version-keyed check.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Patch 0002 adds a check when the server builds an RI plan in ri_triggers.c, on 18 only.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why should 18.x reject these foreign keys at restore time, given that a dump from an earlier 18.x release then restores without the foreign key?
Did you consider having 18.x reject only new definitions while still accepting them during restore or binary upgrade, with 19 and later rejecting them outright?
If 19.0 ships without the fix, will patch 0002 also go to REL_19_STABLE, or what else warns users with keys created on 19.0?
Could pg_dump warn about or flag such a foreign key, so that the user learns of the problem before the restore fails?
How often does the 18.x warning fire for one affected foreign key: once per RI plan build in each backend, or less often?

committability.owner_note: Needs a committer who knows the temporal key and RI trigger code and back-patching policy. Peter Eisentraut is listed as reviewer in the CommitFest entry but has not posted in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change in an 18.x minor release: definitions that 18.x accepted now fail, including at restore. The owner also carries the 18-only warning code until 18 reaches end of life, and the pg_upgrade check for longer.
committability.author_follow_up: The author split the 18-only warning into its own commit, describes the merge conflicts per branch, and offers to add the item to the 19 Open Items list.

priority.reason: Few users likely have such foreign keys, but those who do have referential integrity that is not reliably enforced. The two patches are small and touch tablecmds.c, ri_triggers.c and pg_upgrade's check.c; the open points are back-branch policy, which a committer can settle in review.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the new error texts, the pg_upgrade report format and the exact conditions and frequency of the 18.x warning could not be checked. The material also does not show whether 19.0 has shipped, which decides whether standards-compat-2 applies.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Temporal foreign key actions
precedents_retrieved.summary: A patch series adds RESTRICT, CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT actions for temporal foreign keys, where RESTRICT fails only when a referenced moment changes. Two preliminary patches make ExecForPortionOfLeftovers obey EXEC_FLAG_SKIP_TRIGGERS and add FOR PORTION OF details to TriggerData, so the actions could also live in an extension.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it because the series depended on FOR PORTION OF, which was reverted from v19. He plans to resubmit once FOR PORTION OF is done. No reviewer replied before the withdrawal.

This patch series depended on FOR PORTION OF, which has been reverted
from v19. So I will mark it as Withdrawn for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow foreign keys to reference a superset of unique columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow a foreign key constraint to reference a set of columns that is a superset of the columns of a non-deferrable unique or primary key index on the referenced table, rather than requiring an exact match. An optional USING INDEX clause after the referenced column list would name the supporting unique index where the choice would otherwise be ambiguous.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the semantics are questionable (for example CASCADE behaviour of the extra columns, nullable subset columns, MATCH PARTIAL and UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT), that the change could break existing optimizations, and that it risks conflict with the SQL standard and its information_schema. He said a patch was premature unless the SQL committee standardized the behaviour. Peter Eisentraut said that working out the full specification was the open work still required of the proposal.
matched_queries: FOR KEY SHARE serialization anomaly foreign key
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think the semantics are at best questionable, I think
it will break important optimizations, and I think the chances of
finding ourselves in conflict with some future SQL spec extension are
too high.

precedents_retrieved.title: foreign key on virtual generated column
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows a foreign key on a virtual generated column, limited to ON UPDATE NO ACTION/RESTRICT and ON DELETE CASCADE/NO ACTION/RESTRICT. The RI check computes the generated value. ALTER COLUMN SET EXPRESSION and SET DATA TYPE then revalidate the constraint without a table rewrite.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only reviewer found the patches mostly fine and raised two performance points: the RI check computes virtual columns that are not in the key, and TryReuseForeignKey always forces revalidation when a virtual column is in the key. The visible messages contain no reply from the author before the withdrawal.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_get_constraintdef schema-qualify the referenced table in a foreign key's REFERENCES clause when pretty printing is off, as pg_get_indexdef already does. The goal is constraint definitions that can be recreated on another system with a different search_path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a clearly defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
Reverted commit(s): Add regression test for bug fixed by recent refactoring.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
A view defined as "select <something> where false" had the curious property
that the system wouldn't check whether users had the privileges necessary
to select from it.  More generally, permissions checks could be skipped
for tables referenced in sub-selects or views that were proven empty by
constraint exclusion (although some quick testing suggests this seldom
happens in cases of practical interest).  This happened because the planner
failed to include rangetable entries for such tables in the finished plan.

This was noticed in connection with erroneous handling of materialized
views, but actually the issue is quite unrelated to matviews.  Therefore,
revert commit 200ba1667b3a8d7a9d559d2f05f83d209c9d8267 in favor of a more
direct test for the real problem.

Back-patch to 9.2 where the bug was introduced (by commit
7741dd6590073719688891898e85f0cb73453159).

precedents_retrieved.title: Reducing memory usage of creating foreign key between partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes RelationBuildPartitionDesc build a partitioned table's partition descriptor in a temporary memory context and delete that context afterwards, so the temporary memory is freed instead of being leaked. The aim was to stop the out-of-memory failures seen when adding a foreign key between two partitioned tables that each have thousands of partitions; later revisions were discussed for back-patching to v12.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected early that leak management belongs at the caller level, not inside RelationBuildPartitionDesc. Amit Langote then noted that commit 5b9312378 had already removed the repeated rebuild that caused the leak in v13, so the remaining question was back-patching. Tom Lane found no visible leak in HEAD and saw that the test case was still impractical because of planner cost in RI_Initial_Check, so he saw no reason to back-patch a leak fix. He recommended rejecting the patch and suggested back-porting 5b9312378 instead if a back-branch fix were wanted.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add pg_upgrade check for invalid role references in pg_init_privs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_upgrade check that finds pg_init_privs entries whose ACLs reference role OIDs that no longer exist in pg_authid. Today pg_upgrade --check passes such clusters, and the upgrade then fails when pg_restore grants privileges to the dropped role.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the opening message is shown, with no replies, and the entry was withdrawn ten days later.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Support for upgrading to checksums enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pg_upgrade run between clusters with different data checksum settings by rewriting page checksums while it copies files. The first version did this automatically in --copy mode, and a later version added an explicit --update-checksums option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author closed the entry because reviewers showed little interest in the feature or in solving its remaining problems. One problem was still open: copyFile() has a separate Windows code path, and the author did not know how checksum rewriting should work there. He said the feature could not move ahead without an answer to it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sensing much enthusiasm for this feature or for working out the
remaining problems, so I'm closing this commitfest entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL:2011 application time
precedents_retrieved.summary: Four patches add SQL:2011 application time: PERIODs, temporal primary key and unique constraints with WITHOUT OVERLAPS, UPDATE/DELETE FOR PORTION OF, and temporal foreign keys. Range columns are accepted wherever the standard accepts a PERIOD, and temporal keys are built on exclusion constraints with GiST indexes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut held that btree_gist must move into core first, because the temporal keys need it for most uses. He also objected that the index owns the constraint instead of the reverse, and asked for FOR PORTION OF without triggers. In January 2022 the patch set no longer applied and reviews had unanswered comments, so the entry was set to Waiting on Author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMO, if this temporal feature is to happen, btree_gist needs to be moved
into core first.  Having to install an extension in order to use an
in-core feature like this isn't going to be an acceptable experience.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add basic TAP test setup for pg_upgrade"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add basic TAP test setup for pg_upgrade"
Reverted commit(s): Add basic TAP test setup for pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f41e56c76e39f02bef7ba002c9de03d62b76de4d.

The build farm client would run the pg_upgrade tests twice, once as part
of the existing pg_upgrade check run and once as part of picking up all
TAP tests by looking for "t" directories.  Since the pg_upgrade tests
are pretty slow, we will need a better solution or possibly a build farm
client change before we can proceed with this.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent rejected this fix or one like it. [P1] shows that the empty-range problem has already caused a revert, and this patch narrows that problem further. [P14] was held back for unrelated reasons (btree_gist in core, index ownership of the constraint), and neither reason applies to this fix.
The restriction itself fits the standard: temporal foreign keys there reference keys declared WITHOUT OVERLAPS. The pg_upgrade check follows existing practice.
The patch does not change WAL, the on-disk format or the catalog layout. My only concern is the dump and restore path for catalog state that already exists in 18.x clusters.

The proposal adds no privilege or exposure surface: it rejects more foreign key definitions, adds a pg_upgrade check, and adds an 18.x warning naming constraints that pg_constraint already exposes. The warning fires only at RI plan build or partition clone, and RI plans are cached per backend, so an unprivileged user cannot use it to flood the log beyond normal connection logging.

From the maintenance angle this is a narrow bugfix. It tightens an existing check, and the pg_upgrade check follows existing practice for version-keyed checks. The only objection is the frequency of the back-branch warning.

This is a bug fix that closes a gap in constraint validation. No existing feature, extension or setting stops a temporal foreign key from referencing a plain exclusion constraint, and only core code can enforce that rule. The pg_upgrade check follows existing practice, so this angle finds no duplicated mechanism and nothing that belongs outside core.

This is a bug fix, so demand is not the test. A committer reported a correctness hole (serialization anomalies through temporal foreign keys on plain EXCLUDE constraints), and the restriction matches what WITHOUT OVERLAPS keys already guarantee. The pg_upgrade check and the 18.x warning fire only for affected foreign keys, so their cost falls on the users they protect.
